title: Case 1: Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India (Article 301 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part XIII: Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India • Article 301
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India) of Part XIII (Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India). Relying on the core guarantee that Guarantees that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, dismantling provincial tariff walls and economic barriers to forge an integrated national common market, modeled on Section 92 of the Australian Constitution. and citing Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 301?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India)?
3. How does Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 301 (Part XIII).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 301): Guarantees that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, dismantling provincial tariff walls and economic barriers to forge an integrated national common market, modeled on Section 92 of the Australian Constitution. Applying the governing principle—'Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)) & RELIEF: Guided by Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961), any overreach inconsistent with Article 301 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.

markingRubric.criterion: Precedent reasoning (Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)) & relief

factualMatrix: A constitutional question arose before the High Court Supervisory Bench (Article 227) concerning the scope of Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India) under Part XIII (Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India). While the Public Sector Undertaking invoked broad administrative discretion, the petitioner relied on Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) and the principle that Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free., requiring the Bench to determine maintainability, statutory compliance, and appropriate relief.

modelAnswer:

factualMatrix: A constitutional question arose before the High Court Supervisory Bench (Article 227) concerning the scope of Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India) under Part XIII (Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India). While the Public Sector Undertaking invoked broad administrative discretion, the petitioner relied on Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) and the principle that Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free., requiring the Bench to determine maintainability, statutory compliance, and appropriate relief.

factualMatrix: A constitutional question arose before the High Court Supervisory Bench (Article 227) concerning the scope of Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India) under Part XIII (Trade, Commerce and Intercourse within the Territory of India). While the Public Sector Undertaking invoked broad administrative discretion, the petitioner relied on Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) and the principle that Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free., requiring the Bench to determine maintainability, statutory compliance, and appropriate relief.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Supervisory Petition before the High Court Supervisory Bench (Article 227) is maintainable under Article 301?
2. Does the Public Sector Undertaking's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India)?
3. How does Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Supervisory Petition before the High Court Supervisory Bench (Article 227) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 301 (Part XIII).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 301): Guarantees that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, dismantling provincial tariff walls and economic barriers to forge an integrated national common market, modeled on Section 92 of the Australian Constitution. Applying the governing principle—'Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Public Sector Undertaking must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)) & RELIEF: Guided by Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961), any overreach inconsistent with Article 301 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.

While the District Collector / Executive Magistrate invoked broad administrative discretion, the petitioner relied on Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) and the principle that Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free., requiring the Bench to determine maintainability, statutory compliance, and appropriate relief.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Service / Regulatory Appeal before the Administrative / Statutory Tribunal is maintainable under Article 301?
2. Does the District Collector / Executive Magistrate's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 301 (Freedom of Trade, Commerce & Intercourse Throughout India)?
3. How does Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Service / Regulatory Appeal before the Administrative / Statutory Tribunal is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 301 (Part XIII).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 301): Guarantees that trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout the territory of India shall be free, dismantling provincial tariff walls and economic barriers to forge an integrated national common market, modeled on Section 92 of the Australian Constitution. Applying the governing principle—'Article 301 declares trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout India to be free.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the District Collector / Executive Magistrate must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)) & RELIEF: Guided by Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961), any overreach inconsistent with Article 301 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.

markingRubric.criterion: Precedent reasoning (Atiabari Tea Co. v. State of Assam (1961)) & relief
